figures.finding: No collective agreement sets a Philippine actor's fee; the Eddie Garcia Act (Republic Act No. 11996, 2024) applies to every worker in film and television whatever the role, sets the floor at the regional minimum wage where the worker is hired, a working day of 8 hours extendable to 14 (exclusive of meals) and no more than 60 hours a week, overtime beyond 8 hours, a 10-hour rest between days, pay within 16-day intervals, and full pay for the day when a shoot is cancelled less than 8 hours before.

value.minimum: applicable regional minimum wage where hired

figures.applies: Philippines, all workers in the movie and television industry, from 2024.

sources.said: Section 11. Wages. - The minimum wage of a worker shall not be less than the applicable minimum wage in the region where the worker is hired.

The hours of work shall be eight (8) hours a day, which can be extended to a maximum of fourteen (14) hours, exclusive of meal periods. In no case shall the total number of work hours be more than sixty (60) hours in a week.

The employer or principal shall provide a rest period of not less than ten (10) hours between the end of work on one (1) day and the beginning of work on the next day. This also applied to locked-in shoots. For work beyond eight (8) hours a day, the worker shall be entitled to overtime pay unless it is already incorporated in the agreement or employment contract which stipulates a higher compensation.
If a scheduled shoot is cancelled less than eight (8) hours immediately preceding its approved schedules, all workers engaged for the day shall be compensated.
which shall be paid at intervals not exceeding sixteen (16) days, unless otherwise agreed upon by the parties

figures.finding: The floor in Metro Manila is the National Capital Region daily minimum wage: ₱755 for non-agriculture work from 26 September 2026 (Wage Order NCR-28, a ₱60 rise on ₱695); Wage Order NCR-27, which would add ₱25 more from 20 January 2027, is under litigation.
figures.applies: National Capital Region (Manila and 16 cities/municipality), from 26 September 2026

sources.said: Per Wage Order No. NCR-28 … (Effective: 26 September 2026) … Non-Agriculture ₱695.00 ₱60.00 ₱755.00 … Wage Order No. NCR-27 is subject to continuing litigation

figures.finding: Stage actors have a guild, the Philippine Theater Actors Guild (TAG PH), a non-stock, non-profit body of professional theatre actors founded in August 2011 in Quezon City; it takes members in yearly drives (the 2025 drive closed on 15 September 2025), open to active professional theatre actors, aspiring actors moving into professional work and returning actors, who sign up on its website; no rate card is published.

value.union: Philippine Theater Actors Guild, Inc. (TAG PH)
eligible: aspiring actors transitioning into professional work

sources.said: The Philippine Theater Actors Guild, Inc. was established in August 2011 as a non-stock, non-profit organization aimed to uphold and advance the standards of Philippine theater by protecting the rights of its members. We are an institutionalized national organization of professional theatre actors

Professional theater actors in the Philippines have until September 15, 2025 to join the Philippine Theater Actors Guild, Inc. (TAG PH) membership roster for the year. … Interested applicants can sign up through the guild’s official website. … TAG PH membership is open to: – Active professional theater actors – Aspiring actors transitioning into professional work – Returning actors re-engaging with the industry

figures.finding: Metro Manila (the National Capital Region) is where most Philippine film work is based: the Department of Trade and Industry's background paper on the film industry, from PSA establishment data for 2012 and 2018, finds NCR the main area of operation for most establishments, with few motion-picture production (PSIC 5911) or post-production firms outside it, those mostly in Cebu.
figures.applies: Philippines, motion picture, video and television production, 2012-2018 data.

sources.said: PSIC class code 5911 includes the production of theatrical and non-theatrical motion pictures whether on film, videotape, DVD, or other media. … Looking at the distribution of firms according to region, one can see that NCR is the main area of operation for the majority of the establishments. For certain industries (PSIC 5911 and PSIC 5912), the establishments located outside NCR are quite a few and are also found in major cities outside NCR such as Cebu.
